Compare scenarios: what changed, where, and why

Source: R/compare.R
compare_scenarios.Rd

Compares each scenario in a set with the baseline (or the pairs given) and returns every view of the change:

Usage

compare_scenarios(
  x,
  pairs = NULL,
  areas = NULL,
  area_id = NULL,
  grid = NULL,
  attribution = c("sequential", "shapley", "none"),
  order = c("rules", "zoning", "layers", "parcels"),
  by_rule = TRUE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'plancap_comparison'
summary(object, ...)

Arguments

x

Results from run_scenarios(), or a scenario set (run first).

pairs

Optional list of pairs of scenario names to compare; default each scenario against the first.

areas, area_id, grid

A common geography, as for summarise_capacity().

attribution

"sequential", "shapley" or "none".

order

Order of the drivers for sequential attribution.

by_rule

Whether to split the rules driver by rule.

...

Passed to estimate_capacity() for the attribution runs.

object

A comparison.

Value

A plancap_comparison: a list with one comparison per pair (pairs), and totals for every scenario. check_comparison() reconciles it.

Details

  • totals for each scenario, with the change;

  • sites: the change on every baseline site. Sites whose parcel is the same in both scenarios are compared directly, with a reason code (rezoned, rule_changed, overlay_added, overlay_removed, area_changed, neighbour_effect, unchanged); where parcels changed, the scenario's capacity is apportioned to the baseline parcels by area (parcel_changed). Sites in only one scenario are listed, never dropped;

  • transitions: land and capacity from each baseline zone to each scenario zone, the natural way to read a rezoning;

  • by zone, by height band, and by area or grid cell when areas or grid are given (a common geography always reconciles);

  • land: land in each scenario, and land in only one;

  • attribution: the change split into its drivers (rules, zoning, overlay and area layers, parcels), by running intermediate scenarios that switch one driver at a time: "sequential" (in order) or "shapley" (averaged over every order). With by_rule = TRUE the rules driver is split further, by each zone, overlay or area whose rules changed. The drivers always sum to the total change;

  • inputs: what changed in the inputs (diff_inputs()).

Examples

# \donttest{
town <- exampleton()
pc1 <- exampleton_pc1()
base <- scenario("Operative", rulebook_example("exampleton"),
                 parcels = town$parcels[town$parcels$parcel_type == "land", ],
                 roads = town$parcels[town$parcels$parcel_type == "road", ],
                 zoning = town$zoning, layers = town[c("height_areas", "flood_hazard", "transit")])
change <- scenario_change(base, "PC1", rulebook = pc1$rulebook, zoning = pc1$zoning)
cmp <- compare_scenarios(run_scenarios(scenario_set(base, change)))
#> Operative: 6.4 s.
#> PC1: 4.4 s, 575 sites copied from the baseline.
cmp
#> <plancap comparison> baseline "Operative"
#>   scenario sites land_area floor_area residential_floor_area dwellings
#>  Operative 1,379 1,064,000  2,041,525              1,636,652    16,516
#>        PC1 1,379 1,064,000  2,359,511              1,954,638    19,936
#> 
#> ── PC1 against Operative 
#> floor_area: 2,041,525 to 2,359,511 (+317,987, +15.6%)
#> residential_floor_area: 1,636,652 to 1,954,638 (+317,987, +19.4%)
#> dwellings: 16,516 to 19,936 (+3,420, +20.7%)
#> Drivers of the floor area change: rules +206,799, zoning +111,188.
#> Sites: rezoned 337, rule_changed 376, unchanged 664.
# }
